parts.note: a BBC radio arts show shares its name with the toy tube you peer into to watch shifting coloured patterns, so the 'viewers' look down a tube

explanation.surface: A broadcast aimed at people who watch the telly, the 'tube'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube viewers' suggests television watchers, but the tube is the toy itself, held to the eye; the setter also nods to the long-running BBC radio arts programme of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy is a mirrored cylinder looked through by its users, and the name also belonged to a radio magazine programme.

definitions.meaning: to rouse someone by banging on their door is an old British phrase for waking them
a warm-up rally before a tennis match

explanation.surface: An exciting passage of play on the tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rousing' looks like an adjective praising the tennis; it is the noun for waking someone by knocking on their door.
explanation.definitionFit: Waking a sleeper by knocking and a pre-match practice rally both go by this hyphenated phrase.

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ellis has reworked his story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' tempts as a story Ellis revised, but it is thread: 'revised' shuffles ELLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine, smooth cotton thread used for stockings is a kind of yarn.

clue.text: Priest comes into one's estimate of this Biblical figure

parts.note: one is I, and the 's gives I'S

indicators.note: one piece entering another, so the priest is placed inside the letters for the rest

parts.note: to rate is to estimate
Eli is the priest of the temple at Shiloh in the Bible, a crossword stalwart

explanation.surface: A clergyman enters into somebody's assessment of an Old Testament character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes into' signals the container; Eli, the priest who raised Samuel, is a regular crossword priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the ancient Hebrew people descended from Jacob appears throughout the Old Testament.

clue.text: Duck got by clergyman turning up for some cricket …

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the shape of O

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the clergyman's title from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: A clergyman picks up a duck when it's his turn at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses REV to VER. In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of six deliveries by one bowler makes up part of a game of cricket.

definitions.meaning: a hinged window, which one looks out of
Sir Roger ..., hanged in 1916 for aiding the Easter Rising

explanation.surface: The political views of an Irish patriot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlook' suggests a point of view, but it is a window you look out from.
explanation.definitionFit: A side-hinged window gives a view outside, and Roger Casement was an executed Irish rebel.

definitions.meaning: a puzzling problem that is hard to answer
one who strikes poses, as an artist's model does

explanation.surface: A tricky question, with the ideal reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model answer' reads as one phrase, a perfect response; split it and 'model' is a second definition, with 'answer?' a teasing link inviting you to reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling problem is a classic sense, and someone who strikes attitudes for an artist is another.

parts.note: a US army general who gave his name to the post-war plan for rebuilding Europe

explanation.surface: Someone who plans in a general way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an adjective, but it is a military rank: George C. Marshall, US Army general, devised the Marshall Plan.
explanation.definitionFit: George Marshall, the American general, launched the European recovery programme named after him.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the Roman general Mark Antony

explanation.surface: A comment made concerning Antony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of the surface, 'said about', but it gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A comment or observation is something said aloud.

definitions.meaning: people who keep watch
8 down is a comment, and people who make comments are said to pass observations

explanation.surface: Night watchmen who also pass comments.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on 8 down, a comment: a watcher and someone who passes remarks share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who watch and those who comment both observe, the second in the sense of remarking.

definitions.meaning: in the US a roller blind for a window is called by this name
a spirit of the dead

explanation.surface: A sightless spectre from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind' looks like an adjective, sightless; it is the American word for a window screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a window blind by this word, which also means a phantom in poetic use.

definitions.meaning: a plain band worn to guard a wedding ring from slipping off
a servant, such as a gamekeeper or a doorkeeper

explanation.surface: Telephone for a family servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts as 'telephone'; it is a guard ring worn above a wedding band.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard ring holding a wedding band in place, and a custodian or servant, share this name.

clue.text: Course taken by the first Apollo ?

definitions.text: Course taken by the first Apollo ?

parts.words: Course taken by the first Apollo
parts.note: a course is a dish at a meal, and Apollo stands for any Greek god eating the food of Olympus

explanation.surface: The trajectory of the first Apollo moon mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' and 'Apollo' conjure a space flight path, but a course is a dish and Apollo is the Greek god eating the food of the immortals.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the gods dined on this food, which kept them immortal.

clue.text: Funny thing said in Paris of this learned person

parts.note: a pun is a joke, a funny thing
dit is French for said

explanation.surface: Something comic spoken in the French capital about a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said in Paris' asks for the French word for said, DIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, from Hindi for a scholar, now means an expert who gives opinions.

definitions.meaning: in music, notes neither sharp nor flat
simple-minded people were once called by this name

explanation.surface: A message with pages missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests letters; it is musical notes without sharps or flats. The old word for simpletons is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical notes without accidentals, and an old term for half-wits, share this plural.

clue.text: Silk finish to sleeping-bag carried by hiker

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, here taken from silk

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: A hiker's sleeping-bag has a silk lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeping-bag' reads as one item in the surface but must be split; 'finish to' takes the final letter of 'Silk'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack strapped to the back is what a walker carries.

clue.text: A collection of puny domes -Orwell's description

indicators.note: gathering the letters together into a new heap rearranges them

explanation.surface: Orwell describes a group of tiny cupolas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A collection of' signals rearranging the nine letters of PUNY DOMES. George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name Eric Blair wrote under, a false name for an author.

clue.text: Where Volga boatmen would feel at home on the Texas border?

definitions.text: Where Volga boatmen would feel at home on the Texas border

parts.words: Where Volga boatmen would feel at home on the Texas border
parts.note: Russian boatmen would like a Soviet-coloured waterway, and one such waterway forms the Texas-Oklahoma line

explanation.surface: Russian boatmen finding a home from home in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: Communist Russia was 'Red', so its boatmen would feel at home on a red waterway; the one named so runs along the Texas–Oklahoma border.
explanation.definitionFit: The river forming much of the Texas–Oklahoma boundary has a colour in its name that suits Soviet sailors.

clue.text: Threatened to go out as the note said

parts.note: G is a musical note
uttered means said

explanation.surface: A message warned that something would be extinguished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As the note said' reads as quoting a message; split it into a musical note, G, and UTTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle flame flickers and nearly dies before going out, which is how it is described.

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
an alley is a narrow passage

explanation.surface: A fine corridor aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link here, reading wordplay in definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A low, oared warship of the ancient Mediterranean is a vessel.

parts.note: to yell is to make a loud sound
ow is the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: A colour that seems to make an anguished noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound pained' gives YELL OW, a shout and a cry of hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: The hue of lemons and buttercups is a colour.

definitions.meaning: the proverb waste not, want not implies that squanderers will always be in need
idle, worthless people

explanation.surface: Layabouts who, as the saying goes, are always in need.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Waste not, want not' implies that those who waste will always want.
explanation.definitionFit: Squanderers fall foul of the saying about thrift, and idle loafers are called by the same word.

definitions.meaning: crossbred hunting dogs, part greyhound
people who reel or stagger unsteadily

explanation.surface: Dogs with a disease that makes them unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The staggers' is a real animal disease, which keeps you thinking of dogs; the second sense is simply people who stagger.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbreed hunting dog has this name, and so does anyone who reels unsteadily about.

clue.text: Some heathen ceremony in the future ?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a pagan ritual to be held at a later date.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'a year from now', the word refers to a time later than the present.

clue.text: In an island, the party Venus loved

definitions.note: the clue gives the one whom Venus loved, a noun

indicators.note: one piece placed within another, here the party within the article

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: On an island, the party that the goddess of love was fond of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' works only on 'an', making ADON; the island abbreviation then follows rather than surrounding anything.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the goddess of love adored this beautiful youth, who was killed by a boar.

definitions.note: the definition stands for a place in Scotland

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish first name
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A Scotsman brought up the navy north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reverses IAN to NAI. The definition is loose: a town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the Moray Firth in the Highlands is a place north of the border.

definitions.meaning: the addition sign is a small cross
a favourable point, or a number above zero

explanation.surface: Is this where to cross? Definitely!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross here' looks like a road sign; the cross is the arithmetic symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The addition symbol is drawn as an upright cross, and it also marks a value above zero.

definitions.note: the first name of Ellen Terry, Victorian actress

parts.note: letters spelt out in words: the name for L, then the name for N
the second of the two letters, N, spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: Correspondence penned by somebody named Terry.
explanation.walkthrough: The actress Ellen Terry's letters to George Bernard Shaw were famous, which makes 'Letters' look literal; instead L and N are written out as words, ELL and EN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian stage star Ellen Terry is known by this first name.

parts.note: the saint suggests a knight in chain mail, but here the saint's name is a card sent in the post on February 14

explanation.surface: A saintly knight wearing chain armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' suggests a knight's armour; it is post, the card sent on St Valentine's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The saint's name is also borne by the love card posted on his feast day.

clue.text: Light meals for new students among the rest, possibly.

indicators.note: one piece placed in the middle of another
possibly says the arrangement given is only one way the letters could fall, so they need reordering

parts.note: taken as rest
freshmen are first-year students

explanation.surface: Snacks for first-year students among everyone else, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' gives REFRESHMENST, which is nearly there; 'possibly' then licenses the final shuffle of the last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Snacks and drinks served to restore people are light fare.
